clue.text: A great stop for sailors

parts.note: great in the sense of huge, enormous: vast

explanation.surface: A sailor's welcome rest in a big port after a long voyage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'great stop' reads as a fine stopping place; split it so 'great' gives VAST and 'stop for sailors' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Avast is the old nautical command telling a crew to halt or cease what they are doing.

clue.text: Removed, being absent-minded

definitions.meaning: lost in thought and not paying attention

explanation.surface: Someone taken away while their mind was elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To abstract is to take away; someone abstracted is preoccupied and inattentive.

clue.text: A job for the summer

parts.note: a summer is read as one who sums, and the job for such a person is adding up

explanation.surface: A holiday job, the kind students take in the summer months.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' looks like the season but means a person who does sums.
explanation.definitionFit: Adding numbers together is the work of someone doing sums.

clue.text: Agree ten in new line-up — one's not yet made a score

definitions.text: one's not yet made a score

indicators.note: a new line-up puts the same letters in a different order, like players rearranged

explanation.surface: Ten players accept a new team selection, but one of them has not scored yet.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is twenty years, so someone who has not yet reached a score is under twenty.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone aged thirteen to nineteen has not yet reached twenty years, a score being twenty.

clue.text: Jumper with a pocket in front

definitions.text: Jumper with a pocket in front

parts.words: Jumper with a pocket in front
parts.note: a jumper sounds like a knitted sweater with a front pouch, but it is an animal that jumps, carrying its young in a pouch

explanation.surface: A sweater with a pouch pocket on its front, like a hoodie.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Jumper' is the British word for a sweater, steering you to clothing; here it means something that leaps.
explanation.definitionFit: The Australian marsupial travels by hopping and the female carries her joey in a pouch on her belly.

clue.text: Fools the youngsters

definitions.meaning: a verb, tricks or teases someone

explanation.surface: The children are the ones playing tricks.
explanation.definitionFit: To kid is to tease or deceive; kids are also children.

clue.text: Cargo boat finally transported small racing vehicle

indicators.note: transported means carried away or moved about, so the letters are shifted
finally points to the closing letter of the word boat

explanation.surface: A cargo ship eventually carried a small racing car.
explanation.definitionFit: A low motorised kart raced on small circuits, a straightforward description.

clue.text: Politician in government to mess up

indicators.note: in places the politician within the word for government

parts.note: rule means government, as in direct rule
MP is a Member of Parliament

explanation.surface: A politician in power sets out to wreck things.
explanation.definitionFit: To rumple hair or clothes is to make them untidy, to crease or tousle them.

clue.text: Married with ring, but apparently didn't pay yet

parts.note: O is ring-shaped
wed means married

explanation.surface: Someone married with a ring that apparently has not been paid for.
explanation.definitionFit: Money still outstanding is owing, so one who hasn't paid it yet owed it.

clue.text: Blue study getting Edward depressed

parts.note: feeling blue means feeling sad
a den is a private study or workroom
Ed is the short form of the name Edward

explanation.surface: A gloomy scholar working in his study with a friend called Edward, both feeling low.
explanation.definitionFit: Both mean made low in spirits; a past-tense verb in each case, as in 'the news depressed him'.

clue.text: Came to blows — no longer retained

definitions.meaning: fought, a slang sense of having a scrap or brawl
thrown away or abandoned as junk

explanation.surface: Two people fought and one of them was let go from the job.
explanation.definitionFit: A scrap is a fight, so to scrap is to brawl; to scrap a thing is also to discard it.

clue.text: Gets up in terrible scramble

indicators.note: terrible suggests something badly mangled, so the letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: Someone rises in the middle of an awful rush to get somewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: To clamber is to climb awkwardly using hands and feet, getting up onto something.

clue.text: Withdraw both note and pamphlet

parts.note: re is the second note of the sol-fa scale
a tract is a short pamphlet, often religious or political

explanation.surface: An instruction to take back both a letter and the leaflet sent with it.
explanation.definitionFit: To retract a statement is to take it back or recant it, a straightforward synonym.

clue.text: Informal invitation to sit — not only in church

definitions.text: Informal invitation to sit — not only in church

parts.words: Informal invitation to sit — not only in church
parts.note: a casual way of saying 'have a seat', using the word for a church bench, though said anywhere

explanation.surface: A casual 'sit down', said in church and elsewhere.
explanation.definitionFit: The colloquial phrase invites someone to be seated, a church bench lending its name to any seat.

clue.text: Possibly meant to secure some accommodation

indicators.note: to secure means to hold fast, so the rearranged letters enclose the other piece
possibly signals that the letters of meant could be arranged another way

parts.note: some of a thing is part of it

explanation.surface: Someone intended to lock down a share of available lodging.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Possibly' looks like a hedge on the surface, but it signals the anagram of 'meant'; 'to secure' then makes those letters hold 'some'.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat or suite of rooms to live in is one kind of housing or lodging.

clue.text: Cook makes tarts for demanding employer

indicators.note: cook in the sense of cooking the books, falsifying, so the letters are doctored into a new order

explanation.surface: A chef bakes tarts for a strict boss.
explanation.definitionFit: A taskmaster is a person who sets heavy work and is strict about it.

clue.text: Number of accident-prone vessels suspended

parts.note: a number is a song, about glass containers hanging on a wall that fall off one by one

explanation.surface: A count of clumsy ships that have been taken out of service.
explanation.walkthrough: The British children's counting song has bottles 'hanging on the wall', each one accidentally falling; 'Number' means song, not a count.
explanation.definitionFit: The well-known nursery counting song is about a row of hanging glass vessels each accidentally falling.

clue.text: One to value something that was buried, perhaps

definitions.meaning: a cherished person or thing, someone valued
a hoard of gold or jewels, often pictured as buried by pirates

explanation.surface: A valuer examines an item that was dug up.
explanation.definitionFit: A dear person can be called a gem; a buried chest of riches is also the word.

clue.text: Man (or woman) of action?

parts.note: an action here is a lawsuit, so a person of action is one who brings or fights a case in court

explanation.surface: Asking about a dynamic, energetic person of either sex.
explanation.walkthrough: 'action' suggests energy and deeds; in law it means a court case.
explanation.definitionFit: A party to a lawsuit is involved in a legal action, the courtroom sense of 'action'.

clue.text: Paint theatre group assembled by Hancock's mate making comeback

indicators.note: making a comeback means the run of pieces is read in the opposite direction

parts.note: rep is short for repertory company
met, as people gathering for a meeting
Sid James played Tony Hancock's sidekick in the British radio and TV comedy Hancock's Half Hour

explanation.surface: A painted set for a theatre company gathered by a famous comedian's old friend returning to the stage.
explanation.walkthrough: 'making comeback' turns REP+MET+SID into DISTEMPER. Tony Hancock was a 1950s British comedian whose radio sidekick was Sid James.
explanation.definitionFit: It is a kind of water-based paint once used for walls and scenery, glue or size mixed with pigment.

clue.text: Split over being on board ship in thongs

indicators.note: on board a ship means inside it, so the piece sits within the ship's letters

parts.note: SS is steamship

indicators.note: over signals turning round, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to part is to split or separate

explanation.surface: Someone tears their sandals while aboard a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Split' reads as a verb about tearing the thongs, but it is a synonym that 'over' turns round; SS is the usual crossword ship.
explanation.definitionFit: Thongs are narrow leather strips used as fastenings or laces, i.e. straps.

clue.text: In time, little beast will make mistakes

indicators.note: In places the small creature within the period

parts.note: an era is a period of time
a rat is a small animal

explanation.surface: Given time, a small creature will get things wrong.
explanation.definitionFit: Errata are printing errors listed in a book; the Latin plural of erratum means errors.

clue.text: It's a man out of sorts — this will keep him going

indicators.note: out of sorts suggests being unwell or disordered, so the letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A man feeling unwell needs something to keep him on his feet.
explanation.definitionFit: Endurance or staying power is what keeps a person going through effort.

clue.text: In wars Eric worked for people flying aircraft

indicators.note: worked as in worked over or kneaded into a new shape, so the letters are reorganised

explanation.surface: During wartime a man called Eric served with pilots.
explanation.definitionFit: The teams who operate and fly a plane are its crew, a plain synonym.

clue.text: Song with a melody that's uplifting

indicators.note: uplifting in a down clue means the word is read upwards, from bottom to top

parts.note: an air is a tune

explanation.surface: A tune that cheers you up.
explanation.walkthrough: 'uplifting' sounds like cheering, but in a down entry it means AIR read upwards, giving RIA.
explanation.definitionFit: An aria is a solo song in an opera.

clue.text: Father caught in end of mattress springs

indicators.note: caught in means held inside the other piece
the end of the word mattress is taken as its final double letter

parts.note: pa is an informal word for father

explanation.surface: Dad trapped among the coils at the foot of the bed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'end of mattress' gives its final SS, which surround PA.
explanation.definitionFit: Spas are mineral springs, resort towns built around healing waters.

clue.text: Girl not without heart, but peevishly impatient

parts.note: Petula is a girl's name, as in the singer Petula Clark

indicators.note: without heart means the word not loses its middle letter, leaving only its two ends

explanation.surface: A girl who is not heartless yet still sulky and impatient.
explanation.definitionFit: Petulant describes childishly sulky, bad-tempered impatience, a direct synonym.

clue.text: As a guess, dancing soothes

indicators.note: dancing letters move about and settle in a different order

explanation.surface: A guess at what calms someone: perhaps dancing.
explanation.definitionFit: To assuage pain or worry is to ease or calm it, a direct synonym.

clue.text: Stop being an outsider

parts.note: reads as joining a social group, but literally means going from outside to inside

explanation.surface: Advice to a lonely person to start fitting in.
explanation.definitionFit: To go in or come in is to cease being outside, a literal reading of 'outsider'.
